title: Demurrage and Detention Free Time: dangerous-goods uplift kept out of demurrage goodwill
content:
## Scope

This rule of the AHL Demurrage and Detention Free Time category protects the dangerous-goods uplift contained in a demurrage line from commercial goodwill. It applies to goodwill on the demurrage invoice line of a per-container record and reads the cargo type of the container's booking.

## Rule

The dangerous-goods uplift carried by the goodwill base is passed through to the terminal and is never reduced by goodwill. When the booking's cargo type is dangerous goods, the uplift share of the gross goodwill base is taken out of it; otherwise nothing is taken out. What is left is the goodwill base.

The uplift share is the gross goodwill base multiplied by the product's dangerous-goods uplift percentage, divided by the sum of 100 and that percentage.

## Condition table

| Booking cargo type | Uplift share taken out | Goodwill base |
|---|---|---|
| dangerous goods | the gross base multiplied by the uplift percentage, divided by 100 plus that percentage | the gross base less that share |
| any other cargo type | nothing | the gross base itself |

## Worked example (hypothetical gross base of USD 300.00 and an illustrative uplift of 20 percent)

On a dangerous-goods booking the uplift share is USD 300.00 multiplied by 20 and divided by 120, that is USD 50.00, and the goodwill base is USD 250.00.

| Reading | Share taken out | Goodwill base |
|---|---|---|
| Correct: the uplift percentage divided by 100 plus that percentage | USD 50.00 | USD 250.00 |
| Wrong: the uplift percentage of the gross base | USD 60.00 | USD 240.00 |

The share is measured against the uplifted figure, because the gross base already contains the uplift.
